implementation_notes: Java realizes the link as an object, not a string: java.net.URI is the immutable JDK link target (parse, resolve, normalize), and the producer/carrier/consumer roles collapse into Jakarta REST's jakarta.ws.rs.core.Link - Link.fromUri(...)/fromResource(...).rel(...).type(...).build(...) mints a typed link, Link.toString()/valueOf(String) round-trips the RFC 8288 Link header, Response.getLink(rel)/getLinks() reads it back on the consumer side, and Client.target(link) dereferences it in one call. The classic hand-rolled structure (link struct, header grammar, resolver) is replaced by this type plus the framework's client; the plain java.net.URI + hand-built header form is still justified outside a Jakarta REST or Spring stack, where the URI alone carries no rel/type metadata and the grammar from RFC 8288 must be serialized by hand.
pitfalls: A link's rel is not an authorization grant: Response.getLinks() returns every RFC 8288 link, and code that dereferences the first match or matches on href alone ignores the relation type, so it can mutate through a 'related' link the caller was never entitled to use - select via hasLink/getLink(rel) and enforce authorization at resolution time.

java.net.URLEncoder is form encoding (space becomes '+'), not URI component encoding: feeding path segments through it before URI.create or Link.fromUri mints semantically wrong hrefs - use UriBuilder or the multi-argument new URI(scheme, ssp, fragment) constructor.

Hardcoded absolute URLs ('http://internal-host:8080/...') leak service topology and break behind TLS-terminating proxies: build links relative to the current request (Link.Builder.baseUri, or Spring's ServletUriComponentsBuilder), and keep link targets stable because serialized and stored links outlive the producer - a deleted target surfaces only as a 404 WebApplicationException when a consumer finally calls Client.target(link).

variants.name: Spring MVC URI link building (Location header + WebMvcLinkBuilder)
variants.implementation_notes: Spring MVC builds the same links from the request context: ServletUriComponentsBuilder.fromCurrentContextPath().path(...).buildAndExpand(...).toUri() mints an absolute URI that stays correct behind proxies and TLS terminators, ResponseEntity.created(location) transfers it in the Location header, and headers().add(HttpHeaders.LINK, link.toString()) emits RFC 8288 Link headers; Spring HATEOAS's WebMvcLinkBuilder adds relation metadata and HAL _links serialization when the consumer navigates an API instead of a single Location. Choose it when the stack is Spring MVC without Jakarta REST; the tradeoff vs jakarta.ws.rs.core.Link is that plain Spring hands you a bare URI, so rel/type metadata is your own convention unless Spring HATEOAS is on the classpath.
pitfalls: fromCurrentContextPath reflects the request's Host header: behind a proxy that forwards attacker-controlled Host values, minted links can point off-site - pin forwarded-header handling (server.forward-headers-strategy / ForwardedHeaderFilter) before trusting generated links.

Plain Spring URI building has no rel parameter: teams that skip Spring HATEOAS end up hand-concatenating 'rel' into Link header strings - exactly the manual RFC 8288 grammar that jakarta.ws.rs.core.Link encapsulates.
